title: Bound parents give a finite release-age limit for repelled dust at a fixed radius
abstract: We prove a sharp upper limit on time since release for grains with constant radiation-force ratio beta greater than one. Grains inherit a bound parent velocity and move in a central repulsive inverse-square field. The limit allows all parent eccentricities, incoming paths and release radii. It differs from time spent inside the warm region. For two published Gaia20cdd graphite examples, grains now inside 7 au have release ages below 113.0 or 267.9 years, while their maximum time inside 7 au is 13.34 or 14.28 years. Thus pre-2010 incoming dust remains possible, but the same fixed models cannot deliver primordial released grains to the warm region. The bound diverges as beta approaches one. A speed-ceiling extension, analytic proof, independent orbit checks, aggregate tables and code are included. This is a conditional dynamics result, with no new observations. Gas, shielding, changing grain forces and extra gravity can invalidate its assumptions.

display.caption: The sharp release-age limit differs from the maximum time inside radius R. Both use a constant repulsive force.
Conditional age limits for two published graphite and host models. The radius ceiling is an assumed input.

citations.reason: Uses scalar graphite force ratios and host masses. Adds a sharp bound on release age while preserving the pre-2010 incoming counterexample.
